method: Instruction listings decoded directly from the PE bytes of the identified executable through its section table, with the executable size and SHA-256 verified first. Every cited instruction address, operand, name literal, holder vftable cell and data cell was compared with those listings by a second pass that re-read the bytes. The switchboard listing follows branch targets. Callers were enumerated by scanning the .text section for rel32 call and jmp instructions, so virtual and indirect callers are not covered. Addresses are absolute virtual addresses. The constant switches 0x0057CD90 and 0x007107F0 were evaluated with an interpreter that executes only their compare, add, subtract, move, zero-extend and indirect jump instructions. The MEASURED facts are call-site and script counts that agree with xivl-client-scripts:lua/napi_index.json. Direct call counts, descriptor names, script argument counts, return counts and constants come from a local Lua 5.1 bytecode scan that no tracked artifact carries and are INFERRED. No decompiled body is a tracked evidence dependency.
scope: Static Lua call contracts of the fourteen PlayerBase native registrations that rank first among the unimplemented ledger rows outside the command, talk, emote and push family and outside the records of the achievement rate, hamlet score and chat contracts: _getGrandCompanyRank, _getOccupancyContentsTime, _isCompletedCutSceneReplayQuest, _setAchievementTitle, _countEnableAchievementTitle, _countAchievementRateList, _countHamletDefenseScore, _getNMRushUpdateTime, _getAchievementCategoryId, _getEnableAchievementTitle, _getChocoboRidingGrade, _getAchievementSheetDataIcon, _getCutSceneReplaySnpcSkin, _getStoredItem. Each row gives the registration site, receiver type check, declared argument and return lists with the tag checks, the Lua pushes of every branch including a PlayerBase that is not a MyPlayer, the engine state read and written, the messages sent, failure behavior and yield behavior. Client-side contracts do not establish achievement, title, timer, replay quest, hamlet score, Chocobo or stored item content or server behavior.
evidenceTier: MIXED, see tierVocabulary and the tier of each fact

framework.reference: manifests/chara_desktop_native_call_contract.json framework, manifests/work_binder_native_call_contract.json framework and manifests/fade_actor_group_native_call_contract.json framework: registration, the 0x00CC9D60 type registry, argument marshalling through 0x00D19A20, the holder receiver adapter, the cell tags, the invalid-parameter route, the return pushers and the world object chain. Each registrar builds the return list first and the argument list second.

registration.note: The order of a native is its position among the rel32 calls of its switchboard, counted from 1. Each registrar has one rel32 caller in .text, recorded as registrarCaller. The listing follows the branch targets of the switchboard. The ret 4 at 0x007547B3 is not its end. The switchboard holds 99 calls and the last, at 0x007547BA, registers _getNMRushUpdateTime.

framework.holdersNote: Each invoke routine casts the receiver with 0x009DA6CC from LuaControl (0x01270B4C) to the target type descriptor and returns false without calling the callback when the cast gives null. It calls the member function pointer stored at holder +0x08 with the receiver adjusted by the dword at holder +0x0C. Only _setAchievementTitle uses the non-const holder.

framework.vtableDispatch: A thunk callback has the shape mov eax, [ecx], mov eax, [eax + offset], jmp eax. The PlayerBase vftable cell of every thunk native holds 0x00776340, a bare ret 4. The MyPlayer vftable cell holds the routine that the rows record. The RTTI names of the Lua control vftables show PlayerBase and MyPlayer as the only classes below the PlayerBase holder cast.
framework.invalidParameterRoute: A failed cell vector size test or container bound test calls 0x009D22B4. The target cursor record documents that routine as the invalid-parameter route that ends in TerminateProcess.
framework.scriptBinding: Every native is declared by a _u script descriptor named <name>_inl in chara/player/playerbaseclass_u whose key is <name>_cpp (INFERRED, from the constants of the decoded script).

facts.claim: The registrar 0x0074F4D0 pushes the name literal 0x00FD7F38 at 0x0074F5B9 and installs the callback 0x00706CF0 through 0x007267D0, which constructs the const PlayerBase holder. The return list builder 0x00728C20 makes one int and the argument list builder 0x00728C20 makes one int.

The callback reads cell 0 as an int through 0x005819A0, subtracts 1 and branches to a sign extended byte load at +0xEE, subtracts 1 again for +0xEF and subtracts 1 a third time for +0xF0. A nonzero result of the third subtraction skips the push. The result is pushed through 0x00584F70.
The PlayerBase constructor 0x006ED720 (vftable store 0x00FD5E04 at 0x006ED753) zeroes the bytes +0xED to +0xF1.

PlayerBase vftable offset +0xA4 holds 0x006DEB00 (cell 0x00FD5EA8) and the MyPlayer vftable holds 0x006E2DE0 (cell 0x00FD7900). Both take five stack arguments, ignore the first and store arguments 2 to 5 as bytes at +0xED, +0xEE, +0xEF and +0xF0. The call site 0x00758B3A is in 0x00758B10, which loads the record bytes +0xC2, +0xC3, +0xC4 and +0xC5 as those arguments. 0x006F0220, the PlayerBase override of vftable slot 30, calls 0x00758B10 at 0x006F0269.

The receiver routine 0x0089CD60 is slot 1 of the vftable 0x01057318, whose RTTI name is GrandCompanyReceiver. It casts its argument to PlayerBase through 0x009DA6CC, reads the receiver bytes +4, +5, +6 and +7 and calls the vftable offset +0xA4 routine with them in that order, so they land at +0xED, +0xEE, +0xEF and +0xF0. manifests/data_dependency_catalog.json lists this receiver for the clientbound 0x0194 record under PlayerBase +0xED to +0xF0.

The byte at +0xED is the Grand Company number of _getBelongGrandCompany and the three bytes at +0xEE to +0xF0 are the ranks of the three companies. The roles come from the native name and the argument range 1 to 3.
Any writer of +0xEE to +0xF0 other than the vftable offset +0xA4 routines was not searched for across the image.

The call-site index lists 9 sites in 4 scripts: chara/npc/npcbaseclass_event, chara/npc/populace/populacecompanybuffer, chara/player/playerbaseclass, quest/scenario/noc/noc001. The counts agree with xivl-client-scripts:lua/napi_index.json.
The bytecode scan resolves 9 direct method calls. Each passes one non-constant argument and uses one result.

0x0075EBA0 clears a 16 byte buffer, fills its first 15 bytes with byte i set to 'a'+i when rand() modulo 52 is below 26 and 'A'+i otherwise (a to o or A to O, the case chosen once per byte), leaves byte 15 zero, computes a checksum over the 16 bytes through 0x00D3AB60 and 0x00D3AAE0, builds a record with the type 0x134 at 0x0075EC73 and the length 0x28 at 0x0075EC7B and submits it through 0x004D6D30 at 0x0075EC90.
The checksum routine 0x00D3A380 is table driven with the table at 0x01110808, whose first entries are 0x00000000 and 0x77073096, the standard CRC-32 table.
0x004D6D30 loads the dword at this +0x174EC, returns 0 when it is null and otherwise jumps to the forwarder 0x004E0240. The client architecture page records this as the zone gate.
